behavioral_notes.observation: Registration.state is a 4-value Selection draft/open/done/cancel (default 'open'). action_confirm writes state='open', action_set_done writes 'done', action_cancel writes 'cancel'. event.event._compute_seats runs a raw SQL GROUP BY over event_registration WHERE state IN ('open','done') AND active=true, mapping open->seats_reserved and done->seats_used, then seats_available = seats_max - (reserved + used); none of this aggregation logic is visible in metadata.

An @api.constrains on (active, state, event_id, event_slot_id, event_ticket_id) calls event._verify_seats_availability and raises ValidationError when a slot/ticket combination has fewer remaining seats than requested, enforcing the sold-out / overbooking rule at the ORM layer (not in metadata). _get_seats_availability returns None for unconstrained, applying the min of event-level and ticket-level limits per slot.

Creating a registration or writing state to open/done calls _update_mail_schedulers, which finds event.mail rows with interval_type='after_sub' and either triggers the event.event_mail_scheduler cron or runs scheduler.execute() inline (config 'event.event_mail_async'). Writing state='done' also _message_log_batch's an 'Attended on ...' chatter note. This automation side-effect is invisible to metadata.

event.mail is a time-based mailing engine: _compute_scheduled_date derives a send datetime from event create/begin/end dates plus interval_nbr/unit, and the cron-driven schedule_communications/execute dispatch by interval_type (attendee-based after_sub via event.mail.registration sub-rows, slot-based via event.mail.slot, or one-shot event-based), batching and calling mail.compose.message in mass_mail mode via _send_mail. Pure runtime behavior, not metadata.

register_attendee(barcode, event_id) searches a registration by unique barcode and returns a status (invalid_ticket / canceled_registration / unconfirmed_registration / not_ongoing_event / need_manual_confirmation / already_registered / confirmed_registration); on a valid not-yet-attended ticket for the scanned event it calls action_set_done to mark attendance. Drives the barcode scan check-in flow.

13 JS files, 6 XML templates, 3 OWL components (EventScanView barcode-scan client action, EventRegistrationSummaryDialog, IconSelectionField); 8 registry adds incl. an actions entry event.event_barcode_scan_view, a custom EventMailTemplateReferenceField, the event_slot_calendar view and the event_tour web tour; asset bundles ['web.assets_backend','web.assets_frontend','web.report_assets_common','web.report_assets_pdf'].

This outbound HTTP/api-key integration is gap #7 evidence not present in Python model metadata.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: event is a value network (Stabell & Fjeldstad): its core activity is mediation - it connects an organizer with an audience of attendees and operates the registration/ticketing platform that lets them join an event. The economic logic is membership/seat capacity (seats_max, seats_available, sold-out) and network promotion (event.mail communications, utm attribution, portal ticket access), not a sequential transformation of inputs into a delivered good (chain) nor case-by-case problem solving (shop). It is a primary, customer-facing activity. APQC 3.0 Market and Sell is the closest PCF home because registering attendees to a marketed event is a sell/market motion; the marketing-communication scheduling leans toward 3.x demand generation rather than a fulfillment category.
